The phrase "on top of each other" is a common expression in organic chemistry labs referring to overlapping spots on a thin-layer chromatography (TLC) plate or overlapping bands in column chromatography. This occurs when compounds have similar polarities, leading to very similar retention factors (Rf values) and poor separation. While similar boiling points can cause issues in distillation, the specific wording points to chromatography, making polarity the key factor.
